# PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES

## Central Office of the High Court at the Royal Courts of Justice

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > Central Office of the High Court at the Royal Courts of Justice] 1. The Central Office will be divided into such departments, and the business performed in the Central Office shall be distributed among the departments in such manner, as is set out in the King’s Bench Division Guide.

## Business in the Offices of the Senior Courts

## 2.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 2.1] (1) The offices of the Senior Courts will be open on every day of the year except –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 2.1] (a) Saturdays and Sundays;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 2.1] (b) Good Friday;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 2.1] (c) Christmas Day;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 2.1] (d) a further day over the Christmas period determined in accordance with the table annexed to this Practice Direction;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 2.1] (e) Bank Holidays in England and Wales under the Banking and Financial Dealings Act 1971; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 2.1] (f) such other days as the Lord Chancellor, with the concurrence of the Lord Chief Justice, the Master of the Rolls, the President of the King’s Bench Division, the President of the Family Division, and the Chancellor of the High Court (‘the Heads of Division’) may direct.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 2.1] (2) The hours during which the offices of the Senior Courts at the Royal Courts of Justice and at the Principal Registry of the Family Division at First Avenue House, 42-49 High Holborn, London WC1V 6NP will be open to the public are as follows –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 2.1] (a) from 10 am to 4.30 pm;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 2.1] (b) such other hours as the Lord Chancellor, with the concurrence of the Heads of Division, may from time to time direct.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 2.1] (3) Every District Registry shall be open on the days and during the hours that the Lord Chancellor from time to time directs and, in the absence of any such directions, shall be open on the same days and during the same hours as the county court offices of which it forms part are open.

## 2.2 Omitted.

## The County Court

## 3.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] (a) County Court offices shall be situated at such places as the Lord Chancellor directs for the transaction of the business of the court;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] (b) ‘County Court office’ includes—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] (i) an office or offices serving a County Court hearing centre;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] (ii) the Civil National Business Centre; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] (iii) the Production Centre.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] 3.2 Every county court office, or County Court hearing centre, will be open on every day of the year except –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] (a) Saturdays and Sundays;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] (b) Good Friday;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] (c) Christmas Day;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] (d) a further day over the Christmas period determined in accordance with the table annexed to this Practice Direction;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] (e) Bank Holidays in England and Wales under the Banking and Financial Dealings Act 1971; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] (f) such other days as the Lord Chancellor may direct.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] 3.3 The hours during which any county court office is open to the public will be those published from time to time by, and available to the public on, the website of HM Courts and Tribunals Service 1 , or such other hours as the Lord Chancellor may from time to time direct.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] (Money Claim Online is an internet based service and may be used outside of normal court business hours.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2A – COURT OFFICES > 3.1] 3.4 HMCTS identifies the County Court hearing centre or office which serves the address of a claimant, a defendant, a debtor, or their place of business, or a property, by reference to the party’s or the property’s postcode. The hearing centre which serves the address of a party or a property can be found by using the Court Finder tool available on Gov.uk at https://courttribunalfinder.service.gov.uk/ (opens in a new tab) , or by contacting the County Court hearing centre which supplied the claim form or the application form.
